title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Write X = P^1 − {0,1,∞} = M_{0,4}. Here \hat{π}_{0,3} is its geometric profinite fundamental group, a free profinite group on two generators. S_3 acts on X by permuting the three punctures, and this action is defined over Q. In Grothendieck's notation \hat{𝔖}^+_{0,3} ≅ SL(2,Z)^{∧'} contains \hat{π}_{0,3} as a normal subgroup with quotient S_3. This is the profinite completion of PSL(2,Z) ≅ Z/2 * Z/3, the orbifold fundamental group of X/S_3, i.e. the j-line M_{1,1}. Its kernel Γ(2)/±1 is free of rank 2, and the quotient is S_3 = PSL(2,F_2).

The big groups. N^{!~}_{0,3} is the group of automorphisms of \hat{𝔖}^+_{0,3} that:
- stabilize \hat{π}_{0,3};
- induce the identity on S_3;
- respect the 'loop structure', i.e. send the inertia class of ε_0 to a conjugate of a power ε_0^μ, μ ∈ \hat Z^*.
The resulting character χ: N^{!~} → \hat Z^* is the analogue of the cyclotomic character (pp. 391 and 392). N^{~}_{0,3} = S_3 × N^{!~}_{0,3}, and M^{~}_{0,3} is the corresponding extension of N^{~}_{0,3} by \hat{π}_{0,3}.

This page. Fix the embedding Γ_Q ↪ N^{!~}_{0,3} (18). It depends on choosing an algebraic closure inside C, the element τ (complex conjugation) being the one 'déjà noté'. Grothendieck then pulls Γ_Q back.
- Its preimage in N^~ is N_{0,3} := S_3 × Γ_Q (19).
- Its preimage in M^~_{0,3} is the arithmetic group M_{0,3}, a sub-extension of M^~_{0,3}.
- Diagram (20) presents M_{0,3} in two ways: as an extension 1 → \hat{π}_{0,3} → M_{0,3} → S_3 × Γ_Q → 1, and, projecting to the Γ_Q factor, as 1 → \hat{𝔖}^+_{0,3} → M_{0,3} → Γ_Q → 1.
- In modern terms, M_{0,3} is the étale fundamental group of the quotient stack [X/S_3] over Q. Its geometric part is \hat{PSL_2(Z)}, and it maps onto S_3 × Γ_Q with kernel π_1(X_{\bar Q}).

Programme. Grothendieck says the real interest is M_{0,3} and N_{0,3}, i.e. the remarkable subgroup Γ_Q ⊂ N^{!~}_{0,3}. He states a two-step plan:
1. Determine N^{!~}_{0,3} explicitly 'by computation'. On the next page an element is a triple (h,g,f) in \hat{π}_{0,3}, with (hσ_∞)^2 = (gρ)^3 = 1 together with the inertia condition. These are exactly the 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations of Drinfeld–Ihara's \hat{GT}, phrased as endomorphisms of \hat{PSL_2(Z)}.
2. Accumulate necessary conditions for an element of N^{!~}_{0,3} to come from Γ_Q, until obtaining a characterization of Γ_Q itself, 'plausible if not proven'.
This is the Grothendieck–Teichmüller programme at its first, genus 0 / 3-point level, with the S_3 symmetry and the j-line orbifold made explicit.
errors: The notation is slightly inconsistent: the transcription writes N^{!~}_{0,3} ≃ N_{0,3}/S_3, whereas the image (and p. 391, (15)) reads N^{~}_{0,3}/S_3. The quotient must be of N^~, not of N_{0,3} = S_3 × Γ_Q.
'Embedding' Γ_Q ↪ N^{!~} requires injectivity, a Belyi-type fact. Grothendieck uses it without comment here; presumably it is justified elsewhere.

ideas.what: The arithmetic fundamental group of [P^1−{0,1,∞}/S_3] over Q, presented as an extension of S_3 × Γ_Q by \hat F_2 and equivalently of Γ_Q by \hat{PSL_2(Z)}
ideas.modern_name: Étale fundamental group of the stack M_{0,4}/S_3 (≈ M_{1,1}); outer Galois action on \hat{PSL_2(Z)}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse); Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps in the 1990s
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (action of Γ_Q on \hat{SL_2(Z)} and on Teichmüller tower level 1); La Longue Marche

ideas.what: Group N^{!~}_{0,3} of S_3-trivial, inertia-preserving automorphisms of \hat{PSL_2(Z)} stabilizing \hat F_2, with character χ to \hat Z^*, containing Γ_Q
ideas.modern_name: Version of \hat{GT} with only the 2- and 3-cycle relations plus inertia (no pentagon), sometimes discussed as \hat{GT}_0-type groups
ideas.where_published: Esquisse gestures at it; explicit computation not in published texts as far as I know

ideas.what: Programme: compute the combinatorial group, then find necessary conditions for elements to come from Γ_Q, aiming at a characterization of Γ_Q

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly sets up the search for a full characterization of Γ_Q inside N^{!~}_{0,3}, starting from the PSL_2(Z)/j-line level with S_3 symmetry rather than from braid groups and the pentagon. Whether the later pages carry this further (e.g. extra conditions beyond 2-3-inertia at this level) is the interesting point; on this page it is only programmatic.
missed.quote: il s'agira dans la suite du travail de trouver un maximum de conditions nécessaires sur des éléments de N^{!~}_{0,3} pour provenir de Γ_Q - jusqu'à trouver, si possible, une caractérisation (ou du moins plausible, sinon prouvée!) des éléments de Γ_Q
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Whether Γ_Q = \hat{GT} remains open. Any additional level-one (M_{1,1}) conditions found later in these notes could be compared with Lochak–Schneps / Nakamura–Schneps refinements of \hat{GT}.

deep.surprise_reason: This page sets up a known framework: Galois action on \hat{PSL_2(Z)} ⊃ \hat F_2 and the 2-3 relations of GT, plus the programme of characterizing Γ_Q, all anticipated in the Esquisse and developed by Drinfeld and Ihara. The S_3 × Γ_Q presentation is a nice explicit detail but is standard today.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely reads 'complexe τ ou l'élément déjà noté (τ)' (or similar), not 'l'élément dégénéré (2)'.
In 'M_{0,3}^{\sim} → N_{0,3}^{!\sim} ≃ N_{0,3}/𝔖_3' the target should be N^{~}_{0,3}/𝔖_3; the image shows a tilde on N_{0,3} and an extra superscript.
Insertion above the line: 'de N_{0,3}^{!~}' is attached to 'sous-groupe Γ_Q'; the struck-out 'M' was a crossed-out arrow target.
In the bottom row of (20) the kernel is \hat{𝔖}^+_{0,3} (with hat and plus), and the left vertical arrow is labelled i.
Margin: '[on a une sous-extension de l'ext. M^~_{0,3} de (17)]' — the reference number could be (7) or (17); hard to read.
